rounds.text: Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd demonstrates exceptional operational momentum, evidenced by trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 43% and compounded profit growth of 90% [E17, E21]. This explosive growth is backed by elite capital efficiency, featuring a stellar ROE of 24.1% and ROCE of 23.7%, both of which comfortably tower over sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E12, E13]. Furthermore, the business generates robust cash flows with operating cash flow reaching Rs 1,587 Cr alongside a healthy cash conversion ratio of 1.24x, ensuring that reported profits are entirely backed by actual cash [E33, E34]. Promoter confidence is clearly expanding as insider holdings increased to 62.86% alongside strong domestic institutional accumulation, while the broader Consumer Durables sector enjoys a supportive tailwind score of +0.72 [E40, E42, E71]. Conceded: [E1, E2, E7, E41, E44, E45].

Kalyan Jewellers carries an expensive valuation that is poorly supported by its DCF model, trading at a price of ₹ 613 against an intrinsic value of ₹ 507, which results in a negative margin of safety of -20.9% [E2, E44, E45]. The stock trades at a demanding price-to-book multiple of 10.34x, vastly exceeding the sector benchmark of 3.11x, and offers a negligible dividend yield of just 0.24% [E2, E4, E7, E61]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands a lofty 20.6% earnings growth rate, surpassing the 18.0% assumed in the base case [E46]. Institutional confidence is showing cracks, highlighted by a negative institutional money flow reading, foreign institutional ownership dropping significantly from 26.56% to 10.82%, and an overall institutional holding change of -2.03 percentage points [E41, E43, E67]. Operationally, the company suffers from an uninspiring return on assets of 6.52% compared to a sector benchmark of 14.91% and inconsistent yearly operating margins [E8, E31]. Conceded: [E13, E19, E35].

The valuation metrics cited miss the powerful fundamental outperformance that commands a premium, specifically the superior return on equity of 24.1% against the sector benchmark of 10.03% and a robust ROCE of 17.92% to 23.7% [E9, E10, E12, E13]. While the reverse DCF implies high growth expectations [E46], this is entirely justified by stellar compounding, evidenced by 3-year sales growth of 39% and TTM profit growth of 90% [E16, E21]. The domestic institutional backing tells a different story of smart-money confidence, surging by +10.97 percentage points to 15.83% while promoter holdings simultaneously climbed to 62.86% [E40, E42]. On operational efficiency, the company generates massive free cash flow of Rs 1,291 Cr with exceptional cash conversion of 1.24x, meaning profits are fully backed by hard cash rather than accounting noise [E33, E35]. Conceded: [E2, E4, E7, E8, E31, E41, E44, E45].

The bull highlights superior returns, but glosses over the fact that the company's return on assets sits at a weak 6.52% compared to the sector benchmark of 14.91% [E8]. While the bull defends the demanding reverse DCF expectations, a fundamental discounted cash flow model independently sets intrinsic value at only ₹ 507 per share against a market price of ₹ 613, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -20.9% [E44, E45]. The bull points to surging domestic holdings and promoter confidence, but omits the sharp exit of foreign institutional investors whose stake plummeted by 15.74 percentage points, driving overall institutional money flow into negative territory [E41, E43]. Furthermore, the claim of strong cash generation ignores the reality that operating margins remain inconsistent over the last two years and stand at a modest 7% [E29, E31]. Conceded: [E9, E10, E12, E13, E16, E21, E33, E35, E40, E42].
